short: Symplectic ball packing, dimension 6 and up

title.title: Packing symplectic balls: only two obstructions
title.subtitle: Claim: in dimension $2n \ge 6$, balls pack into a ball iff $\sum R_i^n < R^n$ and $R_i + R_j < R$

plain: Packing balls that may bend but must keep a hidden area: only total volume and a two-ball rule limit you

beats.text: Schematically: disjoint balls of capacities $R_i$ inside a ball of capacity $R$
Siegel and Yao conjectured only volume and Gromov's two-ball bound matter
For equal balls the packable region is the lower envelope of the two

steps: Volume and Gromov's two-ball rule were known to block some packings
Explicit folded packings fill everything those rules allow
The two meet: nothing else stands in the way

achievement.label: Siegel–Yao Conjecture A
statement: \iff\ \textstyle\sum_i R_i^n < R^n \text{ and } R_i + R_j < R
achievement.context: In dimension 4 further obstructions exist; from dimension 6 on, only these two
achievement.note: For $n \ge 3$ only: it fails in dimension 4, as stated

verify.detail: The full equivalence is in Lean: about 107,000 lines under OAI/Geometry/BallPacking
verify.ourCheck: We read the Comparator definition; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: Balls fit disjointly in a bigger one. Siegel and Yao said two rules matter.
Explicit folded packings reach every configuration those two rules allow.
Claimed: only volume and the two ball rule.

sources.quote: For n >= 3 (real dimension >= 6), closed balls of capacities R_1..R_k embed symplectically and disjointly into the open ball of capacity R iff sum R_i^n < R^n and R_i + R_j < R for all i != j (Siegel-Yao Conjecture A).
In dimension 4, packing balls symplectically into a ball is governed by intricate algebraic-geometry obstructions. Siegel and Yao conjectured that from dimension 6 on, only two obstructions matter
the full equivalence is in Lean (`OAI/Geometry/BallPacking`, about 107,000 lines)
The Comparator statement defines a symplectic embedding as a smooth embedding of a neighbourhood whose derivative preserves the standard form, which is the right definition.
Fails in dim 4 (more obstructions), as stated.
